findings.issue: The rewritten SEC-5's absolute wording ('cannot leak a secret') and the redaction guarantee rest on the code-owned producer invariant for ArrProviderError.Message and its transitive carriers (WorkProcessingResult.Reason, MediaMatch.AmbiguityReason, and the ArtworkPublicationResult reason, which is sanitized). Those fields are length-bounded/trimmed but not control-character-stripped at the boundary. All current producers were independently re-verified as fixed, code-owned strings (no URL, key, header, or provider-response text), so no secret reaches a log line at HEAD and CR/LF log-forging is not exploitable today; this is a future-regression risk only.
findings.description: Log-bound reason strings depend on the producer invariant rather than boundary sanitization; bounded but not control-character-stripped.
findings.recommended_action: No Phase 10 action required; accepted and tracked. Optionally route log-bound reason strings through a control-character-stripping sanitizer at the logging boundary as post-V1 hardening.

findings.issue: Every instrumented production constructor takes its log boundary as a nullable optional parameter (`IArrTagsLog<T>? log = null`) and the plugin log registrations are a hand-maintained per-type list. A future instrumented type that is not added to ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.RegisterArrTagsLogs would resolve to the default null (Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection fills an unregistered optional parameter with its default) and silently emit no log records rather than failing fast. All eleven currently instrumented types are registered, so there is no current defect.
findings.description: Fail-silent logging if a future instrumented type is not added to the registrator's per-type log list.
evidence: grep '_log.Write(' src/ArrTags -> 21 call sites; grep 'IArrTagsLog<' src/ArrTags -> all instrumented types have a matching registration
findings.recommended_action: No Phase 10 action required. Consider a registrator test that enumerates the instrumented types and asserts each resolves an IArrTagsLog<T>, or make the dependency non-optional at the DI boundary, so a future omission is caught.
